obs: "For when the question is whether a Federal act overrides a state law, the entire scheme of the statute must of course be considered"
City of Burbank v. Lockheed Air Terminal, Inc.
"There is, to be sure, no express provision of pre-emption in the 1972 Act. That, however, is not decisive."
Hayfield Northern Railroad v. Chicago & North Western Transportation Co.

“Therefore, in order to determine whether preemption is otherwise indicated, we must inquire more deeply into the intention of Congress and the scope of the pertinent state legislation. We turn, then, to the laws in dispute to ascertain their structure and purpose.”
"Pre-emption \"is compelled whether Congress' command is explicitly stated in the statute's *643 language or implicitly contained in its structure and purpose.\""
Gade v. National Solid Wastes Management Assn.
"Pre-emption may be either expressed or implied, and is compelled whether Congress' command is explicitly stated in the statutes language or implicitly contained in its structure and purpose."
"Congress may indicate pre-emptive intent through a statutes express language or through its structure and purpose."
